name: An Experimental Audio Instrument (step by step) — Part 1: Adding Audio Files + Looping

info.title: Adding CSS
info.text: Before we get started, I'm going to just add a bit of CSS to make things look nice...

info.title: Adding an Audio File
info.text: For version 1, let's start simple by just adding an audio file...

info.title: The Audio Tag
info.text:
Let's create an audio tag.
Inside of this tag, we'll add two attributes:

  • src, which is the URL to your audio file, and
  • controls, which displays the browser's built-in play/pause/volume controls on the page.

info.title: Multiple Files and Looping
info.text: We're off to a good start, now in Version 2, we'll add multiple sources, and make them loop.

info.title: Adding More Elements
info.text: ...and add two more! (in this demo, the files are the same, but you can use any sources you'd like)

info.title: The Loop Attribute
info.text:
By default, your audio files will stop playing once they reach the end.

Let's fix this by adding a loop attribute to our 3 files.

info.title: Looping Forever
info.text: Now, the audio elements will loop forever once they get to the end.

info.title: A Phasing Effect
info.text: The looping elements will phase in and out of one another, creating an evolving, generative soundscape!

info.title: You Built an Instrument!
info.text: And just like that, you've created an experimental audio controller! Congrats!

info.title: Outro
info.text: Feel free to pause this demo to play around with the looping audio by pressing the [done] button. When you're ready to continue, head over to Part 2, where we'll give each track a unique ID and wire up a "Play All" button.
